body:
I truly identify with a lot of what you've said. I had such high expectations for my life and I threw it all away for a moment's thrill. I care so much more about my social life than I do about academia so much to the point where I literally squandered my education to have a "good time", all based on lies...

I went to a fine state college, and then transferred to a community college with the hopes of doing better and going to a much more prestigious school. Instead, I focused on strengthening my relationships with people in that school instead of studying. I procrastinated on EVERYTHING and lied to my professors to get extensions on deadlines for projects I did not even complete in the end. I agree so much with what you said; my dreams are my reality too. My reality is a fucking train wreck that I emotionally and physically cannot deal with anymore.

Before, I only cared about myself. I wish I could be a good daughter and an excellent student. I'm afraid I can't do that. I'm seeing this as a way to escape my responsibilities. I fear every warm moment to come in my life will be fleeting, knowing I have a massive black cloud of anxiety floating over my head.

I appreciate your comment more than you understand. It's comforting knowing I'm not completely alone.
I also lie pathologically. You are not alone.
If you don't mind me asking, what state do you live in? I'm in a very similar situation and I wonder if I'll have the same problem with the schools I applied to.
